items.title: Genmab’s cancer bispecific delivers early OS win in ‘exceedingly positive’ Phase 3 readout
items.snippet: Analysts hailed the Phase 3 head and neck cancer results as a big victory for an asset central to Genmab’s growth plans.

items.title: Biogen set up for growth even without M&A but CEO won’t rule it out
items.snippet: Biogen is growing as planned, with marketed products generating more revenue and multiple late-stage readouts expected over the next year. Building out an early-stage pipeline would be a bonus, CEO Chris Viehbacher said on a Q3 earnings call Wednesday.

items.title: New FDA draft guidance doubles down on expediting approvals of personalized gene therapies
items.snippet: The FDA has outlined a process for allowing a single application to cover multiple variants of a gene therapy. At the same time, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has revealed plans to expand the Cell and Gene Therapy Access Model to increase patient access to these products.

items.title: GSK restructure will hit home, impacting 'limited' UK roles
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: GSK vaccine sales miss expectations amid falling demand from adults
items.snippet: With pressure on GSK’s vaccine business, analysts predict the U.K. pharma will face challenges as it prepares for the loss of exclusivity on a key product.

items.title: Lilly’s retatrutide trounces Novo’s Ozempic in diabetes, weight loss
items.snippet: Eli Lilly’s next-gen weight loss drug retatrutide soundly beat Novo’s approved medicine Ozempic in weight loss and blood sugar reduction, padding the case for a regulatory application that’s expected in the first quarter of 2027.

items.title: Astellas bets up to $1.34B for option to advance Audax immuno-oncology asset
items.snippet: Astellas Pharma could secure the exclusive global rights to Audax Biosciences’ DAX-044, an antibody-cytokine fusion therapy that activates the immune system in the vicinity of the tumor.

items.title: Biogen notches 3rd straight quarter of growth thanks to newer products, Apellis
items.snippet: Growth portfolio products like Leqembi and Spinraza helped drive Biogen to $2.8 billion in revenue for the third quarter.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Data leak kickstarts ESMO, BMS reports autoimmune CAR T death, pharma M&A outpaces 2025
items.snippet: Merck stole the show at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) annual conference, with new data on its Moderna-partnered personalized cancer vaccine leaking prior to the presentation and antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT making a splash in endometrial cancer; Bristol Myers Squibb revealed the death of a patien...

items.title: 5 new drug launches that defied industry expectations
items.snippet: A clearly superior clinical profile, reasonable pricing and easy access has helped a handful of recently approved therapies achieve impressive launches.

items.title: Big Pharma is ready to strike, with J&J most likely to buy: Leerink
items.snippet: The largest pharmas have a collective $188 billion in firepower to spend on M&A transactions, with all but one signaling a desire to execute, according to a new analysis from Leerink Partners.

items.title: Leadership Lab: Put yourself first to help your laid-off team get hired
items.snippet: Kaye/Bassman’s Michael Pietrack explores the guilt and grief executives feel when their direct reports are downsized and provides a strategy that helps both the leader and the people who need new jobs.

items.title: Behind the scenes of 3 Big Pharma layoffs
items.snippet: Three former employees of large pharmas, including Novo and Sanofi, share how they were let go. While they appreciated some aspects of their experiences, such as severance and outplacement resources, they criticized a lack of public transparency, a mishandled notification and puzzling outsourcing.

items.title: Biotechs going to market alone must learn to go global
items.snippet: Drug developers increasingly have the option of seeking regulatory approval and commercializing a medicine themselves, rather than accepting an early exit offer. Doing so requires a worldwide strategy.

items.title: After 2 patient deaths and cell therapy durability concerns, Artiva cuts 94% of workforce
items.snippet: Artiva Biotherapeutics, which had been evaluating cell therapy AlloNK for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases, is exploring strategic options that could include dissolution and liquidation.

items.title: EMSO 2026: Incyte a ‘firm contender’ in G12D pancreatic cancer race as early candidate shines
items.snippet: In a Phase 1 study, treatment with Incyte's KRAS G12D inhibitor in combination with standard-of-care chemotherapy elicited an 89% confirmed objective response rate in patients with a type of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, leading analysts to draw comparisons with Revolution Medicines’ zoldonrasib.

items.title: Alphabet’s GV is one of biotech’s most influential corporate investors
items.snippet: The corporate investor arms of Eli Lilly, Sanofi and Pfizer have participated in billions worth of venture capital rounds, but GV is the industry’s biggest spender.

items.title: Novartis faces $1.9B hit from Avidity fail but maintains confidence in $12B buy
items.snippet: Novartis remains "very happy" with its $12 billion acquisition of Avidity Biosciences, despite a Phase 3 disappointment for the antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate del-desiran.

items.title: US biotechs take lion’s share of $54.5B VC money raised since 2025
items.snippet: Since 2025, U.S. biopharma companies have raised $37.2 billion—68% of total worldwide venture capital funding in the industry—with startups in the San Francisco Bay Area and Boston leading the way.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
